title: Relaxed Memory Ordering for Sequential Flags (Publishing Hazard)
pattern: Using `Ordering::Relaxed` when writing to a sync flag or pointer that indicates a separate non-atomic payload is ready.
why_bad: Relaxed operations do not impose any memory ordering constraints on surrounding memory accesses. The compiler or CPU can reorder the payload write *after* the flag write, or the payload read *before* the flag read, causing the consumer to see uninitialized or corrupt data.
detection: An atomic variable write with `Ordering::Relaxed` preceded by non-atomic writes, or an atomic read with `Ordering::Relaxed` followed by non-atomic reads.
counterexample: Acquiring the flag with `Ordering::Acquire` and releasing it with `Ordering::Release`.
source: Jon Gjengset Ch 9, Paul McKenney Appendix C
